title: Supreme Court: State and Commission petitions dismissed as withdrawn
verification_note: The Court permitted withdrawal of the State’s listed 2024 and 2025 SLPs and expressly included Diary 45526/2025, SLP(C) 26497/2025 and the Commission’s Diary 36073/2024. Pagination differs from the original.

title: Calcutta High Court: Shreyasi Dhang certificate-validity judgment
verification_note: In Shreyasi Dhang, the Division Bench rejected the admission-related appeal and held the May–June 2025 re-declaration unlawful. Paragraph 25 treats certificates issued during 8 May–12 June 2025 and 10 June 2025–18 May 2026 as void from inception and requires fresh certification for eligible pre-2010 classes. The judgment records that withdrawal of the State’s SLPs extinguished the interim stay and revived the High Court order. It must now be read with the fresh Supreme Court proceedings of 1 October. The mirror contains inconsistent historical dates for the 2025 orders; the archived orders establish 17 June and 28 July 2025. Local typeset reproduction of the public Indian Kanoon court text; not an official/certified court PDF. Pagination differs from the original.

title: Supreme Court: fresh challenges; appointments subject to outcome
verification_note: In Right and Justice Foundation and the connected petition, the Court issued notice, allowed intervention/impleadment and directed tagging with Diary 54999/2026. Appointments must follow the eventual SLP result, with that condition included in appointment letters. It allowed four weeks for counters and two more for rejoinders, and directed listing on 23 November 2026. The order grants no general stay of the August judgment and does not restore 17% reservation. The listing date is a future direction as of the 4 November review, not a completed hearing. Local typeset reproduction of the public Indian Kanoon court text; not an official/certified court PDF. Pagination differs from the original.

title: Calcutta High Court: Nilanjona Kundu category-update representations
verification_note: For 2nd SLST candidates claiming membership of retained OBC classes, the Court permitted representations to the Commission by 15 October with earlier certificates, the 2025 update and current category details. The Commission must verify eligibility and decide within ten working days after reopening following Laxmi Puja. The petition was disposed of; the order expressly creates no automatic right to reservation. This was relief for the petitioners, not a general reopening of the editing window. The representation deadline has passed. Local typeset reproduction of the public Indian Kanoon court text; not an official/certified court PDF. Pagination differs from the original.

title: Calcutta High Court: Abeda Khatoon retained-class candidates
verification_note: The Court permitted the petitioners, described as untainted in-service 2nd SLST candidates from retained OBC classes, to make representations by 22 October. It required verification of their certificates and prior updates and consideration of their position under Bibek Paria. The writ was disposed of with no automatic entitlement to reservation. This concerns a missed category update within retained classes; it does not reintroduce excluded classes or protect every certificate. The representation deadline has passed. Local typeset reproduction of the public Indian Kanoon court text; not an official/certified court PDF. Pagination differs from the original.

title: Calcutta High Court: Mohabul Islam OBC-to-EWS claim requires affidavits
verification_note: Former OBC-A/OBC-B primary-teacher applicants who later obtained EWS certificates challenged the refusal to accept an EWS category update. The Court called for opposition affidavits within three weeks after Puja Vacation and replies within one week thereafter, with listing before the Regular Bench after that period. All intervening steps are subject to the writ’s result. It has not decided an entitlement to EWS conversion or ordered a general extension of the Board’s editing window. Local typeset reproduction of the public Indian Kanoon court text; not an official/certified court PDF. Pagination differs from the original.

title: Calcutta High Court: Arijit Bakshi representation on invalid OBC certificates in SIR to be decided
verification_note: Justice Krishna Rao disposed of the writ petition, which sought to stop invalid OBC certificates being accepted as documents in the electoral-roll Special Intensive Revision, by directing the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer to decide the petitioner's 4 December 2025 representation by a reasoned order within a week. The Court did not rule on the certificates' use or on the SIR itself. Local typeset reproduction of the public Indian Kanoon court text; not an official/certified court PDF. title: Calcutta High Court: NEET-UG 2026 general-category candidates cannot switch to EWS at counselling
verification_note: Justice Amrita Sinha dismissed the petition of eight NEET-UG 2026 candidates who applied as general category and later obtained EWS certificates, holding that they cannot claim EWS reservation at State counselling (neutral citation 2026:CHC-AS:1271). The petitioners' appeal was heard as MAT 1374/2026 on 18 August 2026, which is not archived here. Local typeset reproduction of the public Indian Kanoon court text; not an official/certified court PDF. Pagination differs from the original.

title: Calcutta High Court: SLST 2016 OBC-A candidates' writ petitions dismissed
verification_note: Justice Aniruddha Roy dismissed both writ petitions (neutral citation 2026:CHC-AS:1414), holding that after the Amal Chandra Das judgment and the termination of the whole SLST 2016 panel the petitioners cannot claim rights as OBC-A candidates, and that the Central School Service Commission's notifications follow the State's reservation policy, which was not challenged.
